Run the staged PIP data pipeline incrementally

pd_run_pipeline.Rd

Runs the durable clean, metadata, and deflate stages in topological waves under one dependency-manifest writer lease. Current nodes are returned as cached units. Downstream waves are accepted only after committed upstream receipts have been reloaded into the authoritative dependency facts.

Usage

pd_run_pipeline(
  inv = NULL,
  force = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("pipdata.verbose", default = TRUE),
  force_surveys = NULL,
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  bootstrap_entities = NULL,
  checkpoint_size = 25L,
  checkpoint_seconds = Inf,
  recipes = NULL
)

Arguments

inv

The complete completed-validation inventory. If NULL, the current durable validation inventory is loaded with pipload::load_gmd_valid_inv().

force

Logical scalar. Rebuild all selected nodes and temporarily use Stamp timestamp versioning. Mutually exclusive with force_surveys.

verbose

Logical scalar passed to pipeline storage operations.

force_surveys

Optional character vector of exact survey_id or pip_id selectors. Selected chains are added to ordinary invalidation.

bootstrap

Logical scalar. Explicitly permit unknown C2 provenance.

bootstrap_entities

Optional character vector of bootstrap survey or PIP selectors. A PIP selector includes its owning clean survey and complete atomic output chain. Requires bootstrap = TRUE.

checkpoint_size

Positive whole-number metadata and deflate checkpoint batch size.

checkpoint_seconds

Inf or a positive numeric checkpoint interval in seconds.

recipes

Optional opt-in M2 envelope with exactly context and nodes. context supplies nonempty release, identity = "TEST", and an existing absolute E-drive root already initialized in stamp. nodes is an unnamed list, including an empty list. Each node requires path, parents, calculation, helpers, constants, semantic_schema, semantic, and lowercase format (rds, qs2, or fst); only audit and review are optional. See the M2 section below. NULL preserves the legacy route.

Value

A visible pipdata_pipeline_result. This differs intentionally from the legacy stage wrappers, which continue to return master inventories. With recipes, a data.table of stamp feedback instead: release_id, path, preview_decision, status, reason, version_id, request_id, receipt_id, outcome_id, failure_class, governing_failure_id, message, and actual attempted. Unavailable proof IDs are NA_character_.

Details

The following staged-pipeline description applies when recipes = NULL. The C2 dependency manifest and exact Stamp receipts are the only currentness authority. The function does not persist a run cursor. A restart creates a new run and replans from the latest valid manifest. Recoverable entity errors block only their descendants. Unknown storage, lease, fence, receipt, and checkpoint failures stop later writes and are captured only after a complete stage context exists. Interrupts and explicit cancellation conditions always propagate.

The only durable nodes are clean:<survey_id>, metadata:<pip_id>, and deflate:<pip_id>. Load, PFW merge, recode, auxiliary attachment, and save helpers are code-fingerprint components, not separately cached nodes. Each selected node is reported as current or stale/forced and then as cached, runnable, successful, failed, skipped, or blocked. Cached clean nodes do not load household artifacts.

force = TRUE rebuilds the complete selected graph. force_surveys adds the selected survey or PIP chain to ordinary invalidation without suppressing unrelated stale work. An absent manifest or unknown pre-C2 provenance requires bootstrap = TRUE; use bootstrap_entities for a restrictive canary before a complete baseline rebuild.

Auxiliary invalidation is keyed. For example, a CPI change for Colombia 2018 refreshes only matching Colombia 2018 metadata and deflate nodes; another Colombia year and unrelated country/year nodes stay cached. Worker completion is not success until exact receipts, inventories, and a manifest checkpoint are finalized. Recoverable entity failures block only their descendants. A later call resumes by authoritative replan from Stamp and the last valid manifest, without a persisted run cursor or an exactly-once guarantee.

The legacy route always uses the canonical auxiliary measures pfw, cpi, ppp, pop, gdp, and pce. Production activation remains blocked until signed target Windows/SMB fencing and immutable unique-rename evidence are complete.

With recipes, pipdata supplies a complete request set to public stamp::st_plan_rebuild() and stamp::st_rebuild(). Stamp alone selects and revalidates run/skip/blocked work; legacy manifests and selectors are not used. Nondefault legacy controls are rejected. All selected outputs are targets, including multiple roots and intermediate nodes. Parents are unnamed lists of exactly path and version_id; pins must be explicit nonempty character IDs, never numeric or mutable selectors. NULL is allowed only for a selected upstream recipe and is resolved by stamp during this call. Cycles are rejected.

Calculations have exactly (path, parents) formals and return exactly one named x (including NULL when supported), optionally metadata, format, code, and code_label. Format must agree with the request. Declared semantic values are passed as metadata; supplied semantic metadata must match exactly. Ordinary R helper closures and complete immutable constants are explicitly declared in disjoint named lists. Deep copies run in a locked environment whose parent is the base environment, not their original capturing environment. Fingerprints are SHA-256 over serialized canonical bodies/formals and values; neither caller digests nor package-version substitutes are accepted. Changes to helpers/constants invalidate the request; audit-only edits do not.

Only reviewed pure base operations, declared helper calls, exact-version public pipload/stamp reads and explicit stamp-classified failures are supported. Dynamic lookup/dispatch, primitives as components, mutable run-state captures, hidden global dependencies, package-internal calls and direct side effects are rejected. This is a trusted declarative callback contract, not a security sandbox, arbitrary legacy closure support, or automatic dependency discovery. Read callbacks must consume the supplied exact parents, not mutable selectors. A guarded public-read boundary enforces the effective parent path/pin pair and explicit physical format before reading. Ambient locale/timezone conversions and unsupported S3 generics are rejected. Reviewed base operations reject classed operands; explicitly unclass reviewed input values before operations. The read/base/closure policy code is also SHA-256 bound into request proof. Recursive guarded operations also reject classed elements nested in lists, so registered methods cannot silently supply undeclared value dependencies. The route checks consumed public producer exports and explicit arguments before recipe preparation, lease acquisition or rebuild; version labels alone do not establish those capabilities. Nonempty recipes require the suggested package codetools for proof generation. If unavailable, an actionable pipdata_engine_dependency_error requests installation in an approved library; no proof bypass, automatic installation or write-side work is performed.

A separate lease is scoped to release, TEST identity, and canonical root; changing a calculation never creates a different writer scope. Frozen proof, root/options and ownership are checked before and after callbacks, including exceptions. A latched guard prevents later callback attempts. Required success proof is read through returned exact receipt IDs and same-pin metadata, never a catalog/latest substitute. Integrity failures raise pipdata_engine_integrity_error carrying actual feedback and causes; cancellation remains cancellation even if cleanup also fails.

Deterministic and unknown node failures block descendants but not independent work. External failures retry only on a later explicit call. rlang::abort(..., class = "stamp_deterministic_failure") and rlang::abort(..., class = "stamp_external_failure") signal the corresponding classified calculation failures; unclassified errors are unknown failures. Review is explicit list(outcome_id = governing_failure_id) plus a real parent/component change; review alone is not force. Governing IDs are recovered from exact committed outcome history across repeated blocks and process restarts. Retained-output recalculation can return unchanged with a new receipt but the same output pin; descendants can then remain skipped. No in-call retry or run cursor is created. This bounded TEST route does not activate production stages or certify SMB, concurrency beyond the local lease, full-suite coverage, or umbrella closure.
